assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: no
daemon_capability: n/a
driver_capability: n/a

## Reasoning

The scenario stresses a LINE-oriented transcript reader with one oversized line. OpenCode 2.x keeps no transcript file: the service writes `session_message` rows into its SQLite store, and the daemon reads each row's `data` column whole (watcher_v2.go, metrics_v2.go) — a TEXT value has no line-buffer ceiling to stress. The column's capability model already declares `file_transcript: absent` (adapters.json), which derives this cell to n/a. Same verdict as the V1 column's 2-16, for the same structural reason.
caveats: The committed transcript.jsonl is the driver's export of those rows, one line each; it is a fixture format, not something the agent writes.

sources.note: 2.x reader: lists session_v2 rows with time_archived IS NULL; a session is admitted on its first session_message activity while a service is up (#2107); an archived or missing row emits EventRemoved (v2SessionGone)
queryV2SessionMetrics re-folds every session_message row in seq order; cumulative tokens/cost come from the session_v2 columns
the V1 column's frozen n/a verdict

recipe.notes: agent_supports=no — OpenCode 2.x writes no line-oriented transcript (store rows, read whole); adapters.json file_transcript: absent. Frozen, as the V1 column.
